title: Obsidian Watch - Quick Playbook
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight, grab-and-go scratch playbook for the Obsidian watch (overnight coverage). Intended to be informal: shortcuts, gotchas, temporary workarounds that help stabilize traffic until the day team can own a fix. Keep this short — copy the most recent lines into Slack if handing off.

Shift summary (what to watch):
- External latency spikes (p90/p99) on hosted-api route /v1/generate when token-rate > 2000/s.
- Batcher saturation alerts (batcher-01/02) — manifests as long queue times + high GPU mem util.
- Model fallback loops: when primary model (redwood-large-ptq) OOMs, router falls back to quantized variant, which sometimes triggers a second fallback and increases token cost.
- KV cache evictions causing repeated compute for chat flows (esp. long-conversation customers).

Three-minute triage (always start here):
1) Check Grafana: obsidian-overview -> p99 latency, batcher queue length, GPU mem util.
2) Look at Alerts channel (#obsidian-alerts) for correlated messages.
3) If batcher queue > 1k or GPU mem > 92%: throttle non-critical traffic via traffic-control (see commands below) and open an incident note.

Quick commands (console / SSH):
- Pager overview: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.test/ops/pager/status
- Throttle route (temp): rdwctl routes update --route hosted-api:/v1/generate --rate-limit 1200/s --reason "obsidian temporary throttle"
- Drain a node: rdwctl node cordon gpu-node-17 && rdwctl node drain gpu-node-17 --wait 90s
- Restart batcher: kubectl -n obsidian rollout restart deploy/batcher-01
- Disable model fallback (emergency only): rdwctl routing set-policy --route hosted-api:/v1/generate --policy "no-fallback"

Temporary workarounds (safe to use overnight):
- If repeated OOMs on redwood-large-ptq, set route to redwood-large-ptq-1q (single-quantized) for a limited window. Command: rdwctl models pin --route hosted-api:/v1/generate --model redwood-large-ptq-1q --ttl 2h --note "nightwatch pin"
- If KV cache thrashing observed (cache-miss spike > 40%): enable prefix caching for heavy-chat customers: rdwctl cache set --prefix customer:<id> --size 2GB (only for pre-approved customer ids).
- If a model variant causes hallucination regressions after a deploy, rollback to previous model version and add a regression flag in rollout notes.

Escalation and contacts (who to ping):
- First: Evan Chu (eng-sre lead) — Slack: @evan | cell: +1-415-555-0198
- Second: Marta Gomez (serving runtime) — Slack: @marta | cell: +1-650-555-0221
- Infra pager: +1-844-REDBOX (use only if cluster-level issues)

Persistent issues to note (for dayshift):
- Batcher-01 has occasional kernel panic after long tail of large token requests. Repro steps in JIRA-OPS-1423.
- Observed elevated token spend (>15% above baseline) when fallback loops happen. Need a durable policy to cap cost from cascading fallbacks.
- A recent kernel update (2026-03-05) might be related to slow GC on nvmm devices — already flagged to release-eng.

Handoff checklist (what to paste into the handoff message):
- Current status: e.g., "batcher queues elevated, throttling applied to hosted-api, pinned model to redwood-large-ptq-1q until 09:30 PDT"
- Actions taken: list commands and timestamps
- Temporary pins/changes: model pins, throttle, cache changes (include TTLs)
- Tickets opened / linked: JIRA-OPS-1423, JIRA-OBS-221
- Next steps recommended for day team: e.g., run kernel bisect, analyze batcher mem histograms, prepare canary for fallback-policy-change

Small config snippets to copy (for Slack):
- Throttle example: rdwctl routes update --route hosted-api:/v1/generate --rate-limit 1200/s --reason "obsidian temporary throttle"
- Pin model example: rdwctl models pin --route hosted-api:/v1/generate --model redwood-large-ptq-1q --ttl 2h --note "nightwatch pin"

Open questions / TODOs (put on day backlog):
- Should the router add a decay timer to fallback decisions to prevent ping-ponging between variants? (I think yes)
- Add a cost guardrail that blocks fallback to higher-cost variants unless explicit approval.
- Long-term: reduce batcher tail latency by smarter per-customer batching heuristics (see RFC in PR #378).

Random notes / scratch bits (keep for memory):
- At 01:12 this morning we saw a 3-min p99 spike that matched a single customer sending 40 large requests; applied per-customer throttle and rps dropped.
- If you need to clear KV cache for a customer quickly: rdwctl cache flush --prefix customer:<id> 
- Don’t restart the node running storage-proxy without telling storage team — causes short metadata blip.

If you read nothing else: check Grafana p99, batcher queue, and whether there is a fallback loop. Throttle first, pin second, escalate if cluster-level.

— Aisha

(End of scratch playbook)
